limitations: Exploratory posthoc diagnosis, not a preregistered endpoint or proof that deleting code caused a regression.
Twenty-four tested cases do not establish global program correctness. Component instances recur across authored projects and are not independent trials or real repositories.
A whole-project execution failure can hide otherwise correct components; unobserved outputs remain unassessed. Missing component keys are observed contract failures.
Unknown final calls remain missing. A saved first repair may still be described when its later outcome is missing; it does not replace that missing outcome.
Component value correctness does not excuse extra top-level output keys; whole-project receipts retain that distinction.
These are finite test-suite partial fixes, not proof of general correctness or identification of a causal mediator.
method: The fixed 28 original checkpoints receive one six-case public batch and a separate original 24-case terminal batch, in the original order. A verified partial fix means the base had an observed component failure and the initial failed patch passes that component on all 24 terminal cases. Follow-up preservation is intersected with this verified-fix set; no model outcomes are replaced.

configuration.access: all inputs from one suite are available to the program in a fresh container; expected values never enter it; shared process/module state within that suite is permitted
configuration.comparison: exact typed canonical JSON values; no token or float tolerance
configuration.model_private_feedback: none; private grading returns aggregate score and disposition only
